_comment:
Claim → proof object. `pattern` is the regex evidence_audit.py uses to find the claim in
. `proof` is a site-relative path to a redacted document image/PDF the page must link to (href or ) wherever the claim is made more than once, or the literal string NOT FETCHED. `anchor` is the section id that owns the claim. `confirmed` is the breeder confirmation date. Empty at the system transfer (spec §1). The first row, `parents-dna-clear`, entered on 2026-09-23 (Known Issue 40) at proof NOT FETCHED: data/faq.json and the migrated pages say the parents are DNA tested clear of L-2-HGA and HC-HSF4, rules/copy.md keeps every health entity NOT FETCHED until the certificate is on file, and none is — so the claim is recorded as unproven, never as proven. evidence_audit.py warns wherever a page repeats it and query_augment.py will not answer a new page's question from a bank row that makes it. When the certificate is on file, the site path of its redacted copy replaces NOT FETCHED and `confirmed` takes the breeder's date. The BVA hip/elbow scores and the PHPV test enter the same way.
_vocabulary_comment: Health and credential vocabulary (parity build Task 20). evidence_audit.py `claim-unledgered` reads every sentence of <main> that matches one of these patterns and requires a `claims` row whose pattern matches the same sentence, or a LICENCE_CLAIM_PLACEHOLDER / LEGAL_CLAIM_PLACEHOLDER. A hit is cleared only by a `claims` row whose `covers` lists that vocabulary id, and a placeholder excuses only its own id (LICENCE_CLAIM_PLACEHOLDER: licensed-breeder; LEGAL_CLAIM_PLACEHOLDER: none of these ids). Not claims, each judged inside the hit's own clause (clauses end at a dash, ; : ? and a comma that opens a question): a question, a denial (not/never/no within three words before it, not across a comma; "not only" is no denial), advice (a clause starting "Ask to see" / "Ask for") and a reference ("page on/for/about the", "results for", "more about the" just before it). Preview pages (board-preview/, kit-preview) are not checked. ERROR on a new location, comparison or blog page; WARN elsewhere. To state a new claim, add its `claims` row first (proof NOT FETCHED until the document is on file) — never widen or delete a vocabulary pattern to clear a finding.
